ministry_ne: कानून, न्याय तथा संसदीय मामिला मन्त्रालय
summary:
The name of this bill is the "Free Legal Aid Act, 2083" (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). The main purpose of this bill is to develop and expand an integrated legal aid system to create an environment where incapacitated persons who cannot protect their rights and interests due to financial and social reasons can easily access justice through quality legal aid, thereby effectively implementing the right to receive free legal aid guaranteed by the Constitution of Nepal (Preamble, Page 1). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

The federal government, provincial government, and local levels shall conduct legal awareness programs to provide information on basic legal matters and free legal aid (Section 8, Subsection 1, Page 5). The provincial government may provide free legal aid to incapacitated persons in its province, ensuring it does not duplicate the aid provided by the federal government (Section 20, Subsection 1 and 3, Page 12). The provincial government may form a Provincial Legal Aid Committee under provincial law to formulate and implement free legal aid programs at provincial and local levels, coordinate with district committees, and conduct monitoring and evaluation (Section 21, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 12). The provincial government may provide support to district committees within its region for office rent, staff salaries, electricity, water, communication, stationery, furniture, legal books, and computers (Section 22, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 12, 13). The provincial government may also provide necessary support to local levels (Section 26, Subsection 4, Page 16). Each local level may make necessary arrangements to provide free legal aid in its area and may provide financial assistance for travel, lodging, and food expenses to incapacitated persons who cannot afford to travel to the district headquarters (Section 26, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 15, 16). The local level must submit details of the aid provided to the District Committee within 7 working days from the end of every month (Section 26, Subsection 5, Page 16).

Non-governmental organizations wishing to provide free legal aid must be listed with the concerned District Committee as prescribed (Section 34, Subsection 1, Page 18). Listed non-governmental organizations must provide free legal aid subject to the working area conditions determined during listing and in coordination with the District Committee (Section 34, Subsection 3 and 4, Page 19). Listed organizations must update details of the legal aid provided in the electronic system developed by the Ministry (Section 34, Subsection 5, Page 19). Non-governmental organizations providing free legal aid must submit prescribed monthly details of aid provided within the district to the concerned District Committee within 7 days after the end of every month (Section 36, Subsection 2, Page 19). Legal practitioners providing voluntary free legal aid (pro bono) must submit prescribed details of the services provided to the District Committee every 3 months (Section 36, Subsection 3, Page 19).

The Council shall determine the quality and standards relating to the operation of free legal aid (Section 15, Clause e, Page 9). The Council shall determine necessary standards to manage free legal aid provided by various organizations and determine the conditions to be followed by such organizations (Section 15, Clause f, Page 9). The Council shall formulate and implement a code of conduct for free legal aid officers, service provider legal practitioners, and non-governmental organizations providing free legal aid (Section 38, Page 19).

The bill creates the National Legal Aid Council to provide policy guidance for delivering free legal aid smoothly and effectively (Section 13, Subsection 1, Page 7). The Council's governing committee consists of the Minister for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs as Chair, with members including the Attorney General, Chief Registrar of the Supreme Court, Law Secretary of the Prime Minister's Office, Finance Secretary, Inspector General of Nepal Police, Chief Attorneys of all seven provinces, President of Nepal Bar Association, President of MuAN, President of NARMIN, one Law Faculty Dean nominated by the Council, two members (including at least one woman) nominated by the Council from legal aid organizations, and the Secretary of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs as member-secretary (Section 13, Subsection 2, Page 7, 8). The main functions of the Council are to provide policy recommendations, approve integrated action plans and budgets, supervise and direct executive, provincial, and district committees, determine quality, standards, and code of conduct, and conduct monitoring and evaluation (Section 15, Clauses a to j, Page 8, 9). Under the Council, an Executive Committee composed of 5 members led by the Law Secretary of the Ministry shall carry out executive functions (Section 16, Subsection 1 and 2, Page 9). The District Committee shall appoint Free Legal Aid Officers on contract for a maximum period of up to 2 years through a prescribed process (Section 31, Subsection 1, Page 17). A Free Legal Aid Fund shall be established to provide free legal aid (Section 27, Subsection 1, Page 16). The fund shall contain amounts received from the Government of Nepal, domestic and foreign individual or organizational assistance, and other sources, and consent of the Ministry of Finance is required before receiving foreign assistance (Section 27, Subsection 2 and 3, Page 16).

If it is confirmed that a person has obtained free legal aid under this Act by submitting false details, the District Committee shall recover the expenses incurred in providing legal aid to that person as government arrears (Section 40, Subsection 1, Page 20).
